messages:
sara: Heads-up — after yesterday's phase-aware scheduling tweak I see a 12-18ms tail increase on small token requests when handshake moves to the initgen lane. Not huge but spikes are correlated with KV misses. Anyone else seeing this?

jia: +1 observed. Quick flame: prefill kernels look fine, but decode-stage queue waits jump ~10ms in the 99th. Attaching short perf snippet below.

jia: ```
# perf summary (sample)
p50: 7.2ms
p95: 18.9ms
p99: 45.1ms
decode-queue-wait median delta vs baseline: +9.8ms
kv-cache-miss-rate: 0.12 -> 0.18
kernel-switches: +2.1 per request
```

marcus: Thanks, Jia. Hypothesis: the scheduler now prefers smaller kernels on initgen but that causes extra kernel handoffs for streaming decode paths. Kernel handoff + KV refill cost adds up. We saw similar in the GPU kernel selector work.

leo: I dug into KV priming traces — requests that hit the 99s often have a cold KV (last used > 6s). Phase split made initprefill cohorts not prime shared KV early enough. We decreased KV prefetch window in the change to reduce memory churn. That might be backfiring for short-lived flows.

anish: Repro plan: 1) run a targeted workload with synthetic short prompts (<=16 tokens) 2) toggle kernel affinity to force single-kernel path 3) compare tail latency and token budget usage. Can run on dev pool. Anyone object?

sara: Go ahead, Anish. If we can confirm it's kernel handoff + KV coldpath, maybe we can relax the prefill split for tiny token requests. Also curious if batching behavior changed (batch-formation thresholds may be starving decode queue).

perf-bot: CI perf-run 2026-03-19T09:12Z: prefill-decode-split branch vs main: mean latency +4.1%, p99 +10.2% (short prompts). Full logs: /ci/runs/7854 (internal link). :computer:

jia: I attached a small trace snippet (stacked events) — notice the sequence: prefill finish -> kernel switch -> decode enqueued -> KV miss + prime -> decode start. The kernel switch (~1.8ms) + KV prime (~6.5ms) is the bulk. We can avoid kernel switch if decode uses the same kernel as prefill for short sequences.

marcus: Two knobs to try: a) token-budget-aware kernel pinning (if prompt <= X tokens pin to prefill kernel), b) opportunistic KV priming during prefill handshake for cohorts with high short-prompt probability. Both are low-risk toggles.

leo: Also worth checking batch formation backpressure: current queue policy defers forming tiny decode batches until timeout to avoid tiny kernels, but that increases per-request latency. Temporarily lowering the decode-batch timeout for initgen lane might help.

anish: Spun up dev job: run id dev-6501, 10k short prompts, 3 configs: baseline, pin-kernel, kv-prime-during-prefill. Will report after ~30m.

perf-bot: Dev job started: dev-6501.ETA 32m.

buildbot: Deployed a quick canary with kernel-pinning flag (off by default) to dev pool (c3-dev-03).

jia: Early numbers (5k samples): kernel-pinning reduces kernel switches by 92% and p99 latency delta vs baseline dropped from +10.2% to +1.4%. KV priming reduced miss-rate but increased memory churn in this run. Need longer run to be sure.

sara: That's encouraging. Plan: 1) keep kernel-pinning as an opt-in flag for canary 2) tune KV priming heuristics to only prime on high-prob short-prompt cohorts 3) revisit batch-formation timeouts for decode lane. Will open a short RFC with proposed default values.

marcus: Agreed. I'll add microbenchmark numbers for the kernel selector change and a config suggestion. Also add a regression test for token-bucket/batch-formation interplay.

leo: I'll dump a follow-up KV heatmap and correlate with request cohorts.

sara: Thanks all. If anyone sees regressions on other workloads (long streams), flag it here. :thumbsup:
